purpose: Primary-report register for additional fighter performance evidence; source scans are linked, not mirrored. Research evidence only, not simulator calibration approval.

reports.notes: All chart BHP values are per ENGINE, not total twin-engine power; radiator doors change between speed and climb. One original report despite two curve groups.
Report describes induction-system leak and poor critical altitude. Not a canonical P-38J production envelope; horsepower per engine.
Same airframe as pre-existing catalog R12; separate experimental sortie/engine rating; avoid treating the two report references as independent airframes.
Military 2700 rpm and rated 2550 rpm climb portions are distinct power conditions, NOT one homogeneous continuous climb.

Water-injected and dry rows must remain separate. Source prose gives 31,400 ft while a detailed section gives 31,900 ft for last speed; disputed row retained with explicit flag. Stalls are uncorrected cockpit IAS.
Captured fighter flown in the US, not a generalized TAIC aircraft estimate. BHP unavailable; preserve full IAS, water-manometer and CAS calibration columns; source needs scan crosscheck.

reports.report: RAF A&AEE Hurricane Mk I performance trials
reports.notes: Rotol controllable pitch, two different loading weights and engine condition; auxiliary climb schedules are not independent flights. L1547 is a different wooden fixed-pitch prop airframe.

reports.report: RAF A&AEE Hurricane Mk II trials, 1941
reports.notes: Performance measurements all Z3564 at 7397 lb; Z2346 not performance. Summary 25,000-ft time 8.8 min conflicts with full altitude table: omit summary time in favor of detailed table. Detailed page spells Z3554 once, apparent typing error; use Z3564 from heading and introduction.
Different rpm, blower and water-injection settings; military 2600rpm climb row transcribed as 2430 vs 3480 at2700rpm is suspicious, excluded from clean observation series pending scanned-page check.
Independent FM-2 specimen. Minimum speeds reported mph, not confidently IAS/CAS; do not conflate normal and overload loading.

reports.engine: Junkers Jumo 213 A/C across test dates
reports.notes: Serial with several engine replacements. Published sea-level and critical-height figures for two power settings. Radiator-flap opening cost of ~32mph applies specific test configuration and is NOT a general drag coefficient.
Two power settings crossed with rack/door configuration. Rack AND wheel-door changes are entangled; not a clean single-parameter rack-drag experiment.

reports.report: RAF A&AEE Merlin 100 +25 lb/sq.in. boost flight trials, 1944
reports.notes: Deepest new dataset: paired IAS/TAS level-speed values and 22-point climb/time. Climb at 9260lb with radiator/oil-cooler flaps open; level speeds corrected to 95% takeoff weight. +18 lb calculations are estimates and excluded. Up to 5 minute +25lb combat rating, 150-octane fuel, not ordinary V-1650-7 standard.

Same airframe as B12: paired increased-boost and methanol-injection speed measurements, NOT additional specimen. Source warns first two sorties had incorrectly adjusted boost, clean summary from report.
